messages:
nina: Quick heads-up — monthly recurrence check. I ran the failure-pattern scan across Jan–Mar and there are three persistent signatures we should triage this cycle: 1) KV cache evictions causing 500s on long-context requests, 2) slow model fallbacks during regional capacity spikes, 3) infra autoscaler thrash on warmup windows.

jordan: can you paste the query/results?

nina: pasted the top hits and short notes: `count by failure_signature, week` + link to sheet https://redwood.company/ops/recur-checks (permissions: eng-only). Summary: KV evictions up ~18% month-over-month on routes with seq>2048; fallback lat p95 doubled on us-west-2 during last two capacity incidents; autoscaler flip occurs when burst_policy=on + node-image updates.

sam: thanks. for KV evictions — is this more workload skew (long context) or memory leak?

nina: looks like legitimate memory pressure from cached prefixes + a regression in a recent quantization library — see PM notes in the sheet. Not leak.

lee: I'll take the KV eviction mitigation. Plan: tighten prefix cache eviction TTL, add mem-pressure alert, and test a slightly larger KV shard config in staging. Owner: lee, ETA: 2026-04-08 (EOW next week).

anya: I can pair on the mem-pressure alert — will add a sample alert rule and a dashboard.

jordan: for model fallback slowness, ops-bot shows two fallbacks during capacity spike on 2026-03-15 and 2026-03-19. We should consider a faster routing policy or keep a small warm pool for critical customers. Owner suggestion: sam (routing) + infra-owner for warm pool.

sam: i'll own routing policy changes. Quick win: reduce failure detection window from 30s -> 12s for the routing health check for high-priority routes. I'll open an RFC with metrics needed and a canary plan. ETA: 2026-04-15.

jordan: who owns warm pool infra? ops-bot, any infra lead?

incident-bot: @infra-leads — warm pool capacity topic flagged by recurrence analysis. (automated note)
